title: Investigate adaptive padding regression in streaming path causing tokens/sec collapse
creator: Maya Singh
description: Production incidents across Hosted and Dedicated customers show an abrupt collapse in tokens/sec for streaming generation after the adaptive-padding optimizer roll-out (runtime-1.32). TTFT for long-context streaming requests increased and aggregate throughput dropped ~45% for mixed-length workloads. Private deployments reported the same behavior when they enabled the new padding mode in their config. This ticket tracks root-cause investigation, mitigations, and the hotfix rollout.
reproduce_steps: 1) Run streaming generation workload with mixed prompt lengths (short prompts + occasional long prompts) against runtime-1.32 with adaptive padding enabled
2) Observe scheduler behavior: batch sizes shrink and more single-request microbatches appear during bursts
3) Measure tokens/sec on worker: expected ~12k tok/s, observed ~6.5k tok/s; TTFT increase of 120-250ms depending on model and region
4) Confirm toggling adaptive_padding=false on a canary host returns batching patterns and tokens/sec to baseline
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:20 UTC - Pager triggered by large ecommerce customer complaining of 2x cost and 2x latency on streaming chat flows (Hosted - us-west).

Telemetry shows sudden increase in inter-request variance and a flood of small batches coinciding with adaptive padding rollout that changed padding heuristics to per-request dynamic padding based on recent sequence distribution.

Root hypothesis: adaptive padding misestimates effective sequence length in mixed workloads causing scheduler to treat streams as variable-length and avoid coalescing, which reduces batching efficiency and throughput.

Observed across model variants: q4_0 quantized 13B and q8_0 7B show impact; float32 models affected but less severe. Private customers on the same runtime package saw identical regression after toggling feature flag on their nodes.
Heap and CPU usage on workers remain stable; the issue is scheduling/packing inefficiency rather than kernel slowdown.

Cross-check: K/V cache and kernel selector recent changes are unrelated (no concurrent deploys on affected clusters), but a timing change in stream-heartbeat and the new padding estimator together exacerbate fragmentation of batch windows.
mitigation_plan: 1) Immediate config-level mitigation: set adaptive_padding=false on affected pools (Hosted canaries and Dedicated critical pools) — executed 2026-03-12 11:04 UTC.
2) Hotfix: patch scheduler to fall back to size-based coalescing when per-request padding would produce microbatches (PR linked below).
3) Longer-term: replace current estimator with a conservative percentile-based estimator and add hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping on mixed workloads.
4) Communication: notify impacted customers and CS with mitigation status and expected rollback timeframes.
rollout_plan: Canary (small Dedicated pool + Hosted canaries) - apply scheduler patch and set adaptive_padding=true with patch monitoring - target: 2% traffic - 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC
Ramp to 25% - monitor tokens/sec, P50/P95 TTFT, batch size distribution - 24h
If stable, ramp to 100% across Hosted and push declarative guidance for Dedicated customers; Publish private deployment hotfix package and helm chart patch for self-hosted installs.
Rollback plan: set adaptive_padding=false globally if metrics regress beyond 10% from baseline or errors spike.
monitoring_and_metrics: Primary KPIs: aggregate tokens/sec (cluster-level), TTFT P50/P95, average batch size, microbatch ratio (batches < 3 requests)
Baseline (pre-regression): tokens/sec ~12000 tok/s for mixed workload, avg batch size 6. Post-regression observed ~6500 tok/s, avg batch size 2.3, microbatch ratio > 60%
Dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/runtime/perf/streams?cluster=us-west (canary link), keep-alerts enabled for >20% throughput drop
Synthetic smoke tests added to CI to validate batch coalescing for mixed-length streaming cases.
